meanings.en: thus, in this way, like this
meanings.note: Ainsi que = as well as. Invariable French adverb meaning 'thus'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.trans: It was not planned like this.

examples.text: Ce déjeuner n'était pas prévu ainsi.
examples.trans: This lunch was not planned this way.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'after'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
Après le déjeuner. Invariable French adverb meaning 'after'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Après, elles ne peuvent plus s'arrêter.
On mange, et après on part.
examples.trans: We eat, and afterwards we leave.

examples.text: Elles commencent avec un peu de Botox. Après, elles ne peuvent plus s'arrêter.
examples.trans: They start with a bit of Botox. Then they can't stop anymore.

meanings.note: j'en ai assez = I've had enough, I'm fed up
Assez bien. Invariable French adverb meaning 'enough'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.trans: I've got a problem at work.

meanings.note: avoir peur = to be afraid, avoir raison = to be right, avoir 40 ans = to be 40

meanings.en: helper verb of the passé composé
meanings.note: J'ai appelé = I called. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.

meanings.en: il y a = there is, there are
meanings.note: Fixed expression. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.
un cadeau d'anniversaire = a birthday present

examples.text: Il m'apportait un cadeau et passait du temps avec moi.
examples.trans: He would bring me a gift and spend time with me.
It is a present for you.

meanings.note: determiner: ce soir = tonight, cette semaine = this week
pronoun: c'est = it is; tout ce que = all that

examples.text: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
Cette agence ne représente que des stars.
Magali, je dois voir la pièce de Koltès cette semaine.
examples.trans: Magali, I have to see the Koltès play this week.

meanings.note: D' before a vowel. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
le film de Tarantino = Tarantino's film
Also 'some': du sucre. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Masculine noun ('le degré', plural 'les degrés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'degree'.

examples.text: Il faut prendre cette blague au second degré.
examples.trans: You have to take this joke with a grain of irony.
The water heats up to a hundred degrees.

meanings.note: Spoken French diʁɛktəmɑ̃ expression meaning 'directly', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Pourquoi il ne m'appelle pas directement?
examples.trans: Why doesn't he call me directly?

examples.text: Alors pourquoi il ne m'appelle pas directement?
examples.trans: Then why doesn't he call me directly?

meanings.note: Physically hard, or hard to bear. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'hard'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
C'est dur = it's tough. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'hard'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Je comprends. C'est un coup dur.
examples.trans: I understand. It's a real blow.

meanings.note: Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation.

examples.text: Elle est débordée, ne l'embêtons pas.
examples.trans: She is swamped, let's not bother her.

meanings.note: en retard = late, en vacances = on holiday

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

meanings.note: masculine or feminine: un enfant, une enfant

examples.text: Je voulais un enfant, et pas elle.
examples.trans: I wanted a child, and she didn't.

meanings.note: c'est facile de + infinitive: it's easy to

examples.text: Non, c'est facile de dire terminé.
examples.trans: No, it's easy to say done.

meanings.note: for (duration): ça fait des mois que j'attends = I've been waiting for months

meanings.note: Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to do, to make'.

meanings.note: With time. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to do, to make'.

examples.text: Ça fait une heure que j'attends.
examples.trans: I've been waiting for an hour.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le film', plural 'les films') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'film'.

examples.text: C'est le prochain film de Tarantino.
Tu as le film de Kechiche.
Vous tournez un film aux États-Unis?
examples.trans: Are you making a film in the United States?

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'feline'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Il écrit que ma beauté féline le hante.
examples.trans: He writes that my feline beauty haunts him.

meanings.note: Faire la fête = to party. Feminine noun ('la fête', plural 'les fêtes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'party'.

examples.text: On fait la fête ce soir!

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'here'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Laissez vos photos et votre CV ici.
examples.trans: Leave your photos and your CV here.

meanings.note: for masculine nouns, and in impersonal phrases: il y a
Also in fixed phrases: il y a. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'he'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
Never changes for plural. Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'there is', common in natural conversation.
il y a trois semaines = three weeks ago

examples.text: Il y a une autre Clémentine?
Non, c'est la place de Samuel. Il est mort il y a six jours.
examples.trans: No, it's Samuel's place. He died six days ago.

meanings.note: J' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'I'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: jouer un rôle, jouer le frère de...
Je joue dans un spectacle. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to play'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'joué').
Jouer au foot, jouer du piano. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to play'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'joué').

examples.text: Il joue le frère de Guillaume.

meanings.note: definite article; l' before a vowel

examples.text: C'est le prochain film de Tarantino.

meanings.note: Mais oui! = of course!. French conjunction meaning 'but', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.

meanings.en: en avoir marre (de) = to be fed up (with), to be sick of
meanings.note: Casual everyday idiom. Invariable French adverb meaning 'fed up'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: C'est pour moi? J'en ai marre.
examples.trans: Is that aimed at me? I'm fed up.

meanings.note: ma before a feminine noun, mon before a vowel

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: ne... pas = not; ne... rien = nothing; ne... que = only; n' before a vowel

occuper.gloss: to occupy; to take care of

meanings.en: s'occuper de = to take care of, to deal with
meanings.note: Occupe-toi de... = take care of. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to occupy'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'occupé').
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to occupy'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'occupé').

examples.text: Je dois m'occuper de la musique. Profite de l'ambiance.

meanings.note: everyday speech, with a he/she verb form
General. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'we'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: On est au Westin. Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.en: to organize, to arrange, to set up
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to organize'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'organisé').

examples.trans: I want to set up a meeting.

meanings.en: to go home, to get back
meanings.note: Passé composé with être. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to go home'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'rentré').

meanings.en: to start again, to resume, to pick up
